questions.prompt: Walk through how a signed-in request to Stockade's /data/health endpoint ends up counting only its own merchant's rows: where does the merchant identifier come from, which gate runs before the health branch, and why is scoping enforced per query rather than once?

keyPoints.text: Session.Account parses BOTH the account-id claim and the merchant claim from the cookie principal; either one missing or malformed is refused as unauthorized.
It then loads the single account row whose id and merchant match the pair together, so a cookie mixing one merchant's account with another merchant's claim resolves to nothing.
The Actor that every read uses copies MerchantId from that loaded account row, so the scope value is the database's answer, not a client-supplied parameter.
Before the health branch is reached the list endpoint has already passed Demand("owner", "admin"), so support and warehouse roles get a 403 rather than the operational counts.
Each count is its own CountAsync with its own MerchantId == a.MerchantId predicate; nothing applies the scope once for the branch, so every query has to carry it.
Getting the classification right is not enough on its own: tenancy is a second, independent condition on the same query.
keyPoints.quote: Merchant scoping is another independent predicate.

keyPoints.text: A count that forgets the scope is still arithmetically correct, which is exactly why it is dangerous: it reports other tenants' work as yours.
keyPoints.quote: Correct arithmetic over the entire table would still leak another merchant's operational information.

questions.prompt: Explain where the twelve-attempt line sits in Stockade's refund recovery loop: how does the background worker pick refunds and move their counter, how does an operator move a refund back, and what must stay true for the health partition to describe that loop honestly?

keyPoints.text: The worker's refund pass selects pending rows under the attempt ceiling with no merchant filter: it is a cross-tenant recovery process, unlike the per-merchant read.
Each refund is processed under a PostgreSQL advisory lock keyed by its id, and a refund that is no longer pending when re-read is skipped.
A provider failure leaves the refund pending and bumps its Attempts in a separate transaction; a success moves the amount from RefundPending into Refunded and marks it succeeded.

The operator path is RetryRefund: owner/admin only, a reason is required, a non-pending refund is refused with refund_state, and the counter goes back to zero so the worker's selection picks it up again.
The partition is a split of one merchant's pending set at twelve into two non-overlapping halves.
keyPoints.quote: Divide that set at twelve attempts.

keyPoints.text: State is a separate filter from the counter: a refund that already succeeded keeps its historical attempts and must not be read as recovery work.
keyPoints.quote: State and attempt count both matter.

keyPoints.text: The health split is only meaningful while its threshold is the same one the worker selects on; the read side and the worker side each spell the number out separately.

questions.prompt: Defend or indict this claim about Stockade's operational health panel: "the dashboard is where operators recover stuck refunds." Say what the panel renders, what it can actually trigger, and where the real recovery authority lives.

keyPoints.text: healthStats is a pure mapping from the response to label/value pairs; the exhausted-refund card only adds a help string, it carries no handler.
The worked change says so outright: the new card is guidance and grants nothing.
The help text is rendered as a title tooltip on the stat tile; clicking a tile submits nothing.
The one action the panel does own is Reconcile now, which posts /reconcile, and that endpoint re-checks owner/admin on the server before running.
The recovery itself is a command routed through Commerce, which resolves the refund with Get<T> scoped by the actor's MerchantId, so another tenant's refund id answers not_found.
The presentation test pins the separation: the retryable and exhausted tiles stay distinct and the exhausted one keeps help that names the action.
So the claim is wrong: the panel reports and points; the authority stays with the server-side, role-checked, merchant-scoped command.
keyPoints.quote: Its contract is correct per-query classification and account scope.
